meta.sampling: stratified by framework, round-robin by category

bugs.title: Wrong embedding gradients with distributed optimizer and shared embedding
bugs.description: When use_distributed_optimizer + share_embeddings_and_output_weights, embedding gradients are reduce-scattered across DP ranks before being all-reduced across PP stages, causing partial results to be summed incorrectly. wte and lm_head grads end up on different DP ranks, producing wrong embedding gradients.
bugs.root_cause: When use_distributed_optimizer + share_embeddings_and_output_weights, embedding gradients are reduce-scattered across DP ranks before being all-reduced across PP stages, causing partial results to be summed incorrectly. wte and lm_head grads end up on different DP ranks, producing wrong embedding gradients.

bugs.title: Fix: Initialize master_weight with params_dtype directly
bugs.description: Master weights are initialized by first creating in one dtype then casting, instead of directly using params_dtype. The unnecessary casting introduces numerical precision loss during initialization, affecting mixed-precision training.
bugs.root_cause: Master weights are initialized by first creating in one dtype then casting, instead of directly using params_dtype. The unnecessary casting introduces numerical precision loss during initialization, affecting mixed-precision training.

bugs.title: Tensor parallelism produces divergent loss with non-divisible vocabulary sizes
bugs.description: When vocabulary size is not evenly divisible by TP size, uneven vocab splits cause systematic loss divergence. After 2000 steps, absolute error reaches 47.137 (>50% relative error) vs single-GPU training.
bugs.root_cause: When vocabulary size is not evenly divisible by TP size, uneven vocab splits cause systematic loss divergence. After 2000 steps, absolute error reaches 47.137 (>50% relative error) vs single-GPU training.

bugs.title: Stale weights used with --overlap-param-gather when bucket order differs from forward order
bugs.description: When parameter bucket order differs from model forward execution order, all-gather hasn't completed for a bucket before its parameters are used in forward. The previous step's weights are used, producing incorrect results.
bugs.root_cause: When parameter bucket order differs from model forward execution order, all-gather hasn't completed for a bucket before its parameters are used in forward. The previous step's weights are used, producing incorrect results.

bugs.title: calculate_per_token_loss with CP misses context_parallel_size scale factor
bugs.root_cause: In pretrain_gpt.py loss_func and pipeline schedules.forward_step, the loss was multiplied by args.context_parallel_size only when not using calculate_per_token_loss. With per-token loss the CP factor was missing, so when CP later divided again the resulting gradient was off by 1/cp_size.
bugs.invariant: Final scaled loss passed to backward must equal local_loss * cp_world_size / num_microbatches in both calculate_per_token_loss=True and False modes.

bugs.title: Learning rate not overridden when set --override-opt_param-scheduler
bugs.description: When loading a checkpoint with --override-opt_param-scheduler and new LR params, the get_lr method still retrieves max_lr/min_lr from param_group (old values), ignoring the override. LR scheduler state persists incorrectly.
bugs.root_cause: When loading a checkpoint with --override-opt_param-scheduler and new LR params, the get_lr method still retrieves max_lr/min_lr from param_group (old values), ignoring the override. LR scheduler state persists incorrectly.

bugs.title: SwitchMLP router torch.nn.Linear init not wrapped in data-parallel RNG tracker
bugs.root_cause: Buggy init does `self.router = torch.nn.Linear(...)` outside of any RNG tracker fork. If the default CUDA RNG state is asymmetric across TP ranks at the point of router construction, weights diverge. Fix wraps init in `get_cuda_rng_tracker().fork(get_data_parallel_rng_tracker_name())`.
bugs.invariant: During SwitchMLP construction, the router's weight init must execute inside a get_cuda_rng_tracker().fork(<data-parallel name>) context

bugs.title: GPTDataset returns aliased cached_loss_mask, downstream in-place padding mutates the shared cache and corrupts later samples
bugs.root_cause: In the cached-mask branch, GPTDataset assigned loss_mask = self.cached_loss_mask, returning the cached tensor by reference instead of a clone. Downstream code in the same __getitem__ path applies in-place modifications (e.g. zeroing the loss for pad tokens). The first sample with padding silently mutates the shared cache, so every subsequent sample served from the cache starts from a polluted mask.
bugs.invariant: GPTDataset.cached_loss_mask must equal a tensor of all-ones at the start of every __getitem__ call.
trigger_conditions: create_attention_mask=False so the cached-mask branch is taken
Sequences with padding so loss_mask is mutated per-sample by mask_loss_or_position fill

bugs.title: Loss not decreasing when using overlap-param-gather with overlap-grad-reduce
bugs.description: When both --overlap-param-gather and --overlap-grad-reduce are enabled simultaneously, found_inf_flag stays true causing learning rate to remain at zero. Training loop runs but no meaningful learning occurs.
bugs.root_cause: All-gather handle list in DistributedOptimizer not properly initialized. Causes stale handles, which makes FP16 loss scaler always detect inf, setting LR=0 and skipping all parameter updates.
bugs.invariant: After warmup, learning_rate > 0 and loss must decrease. All iterations skipped or LR=0 = bug.

bugs.title: Optimizer offload checkpoint loading causes loss to jump from 0.31 to 10
bugs.description: With --use-precision-aware-optimizer and --optimizer-cpu-offload, resuming from checkpoint causes loss to jump dramatically (0.31 -> 10). Optimizer state is corrupted during serialization/deserialization with CPU offloading active.
bugs.root_cause: With --use-precision-aware-optimizer and --optimizer-cpu-offload, resuming from checkpoint causes loss to jump dramatically (0.31 -> 10). Optimizer state is corrupted during serialization/deserialization with CPU offloading active.

bugs.title: Incorrect loss scaling in context parallel code logic
bugs.description: Loss is multiplied by cp_size in the backward pass, causing gradient outputs to differ from non-CP training. The mul cp_size logic should be removed; gradients should use the chunk's local loss, not the all-reduced loss.
bugs.root_cause: Loss is multiplied by cp_size in the backward pass, causing gradient outputs to differ from non-CP training. The mul cp_size logic should be removed; gradients should use the chunk's local loss, not the all-reduced loss.

bugs.title: Wrong attention gradient when Context Parallelism is on
bugs.description: dQ, dK, dV output from the backward function of core_attention are wrong when context parallelism is enabled. Activation gradients have relative error as large as 1.2 compared to single-card training.
bugs.root_cause: dQ, dK, dV output from the backward function of core_attention are wrong when context parallelism is enabled. Activation gradients have relative error as large as 1.2 compared to single-card training.

bugs.title: TopKRouter expert_bias gets wrong dtype (bf16 instead of fp32)
bugs.description: expert_bias buffer is registered as fp32 but silently cast to bf16 during forward pass and finalize_model_grads when training with --bf16. This causes precision loss in bias updates that occur at very small rates.
bugs.root_cause: Float16Module converts all registered buffers to bf16/fp16. expert_bias is a fp32 buffer that gets silently downcast, causing precision loss in routing decisions.
bugs.invariant: expert_bias.dtype must be torch.float32 during routing. bf16/fp16 = bug.

bugs.title: Fix error in pipeline-parallel schedules to support context parallel
bugs.description: get_tensor_shapes() in schedules.py doesn't account for context parallel size, producing wrong tensor shapes for p2p communication between pipeline stages when CP is enabled.
bugs.root_cause: get_tensor_shapes() in schedules.py doesn't account for context parallel size, producing wrong tensor shapes for p2p communication between pipeline stages when CP is enabled.

bugs.root_cause: ga_steps > 1 条件阻止了 ga_steps=1 但有多次 backward 场景的梯度累积，中间 backward 的梯度被丢弃，参数偏差达 2e-3

bugs.title: Sparse gradients silently not updating — SparseTensor wraps .data instead of param.grad
bugs.root_cause: In _get_gradients_for_reduction, the sparse-gradient branch wrapped `param.grad.data` into a SparseTensor: `grad_data = SparseTensor(grad_data)`. Because Python re-bound the local name and never wrote back into param.grad, the post-allreduce updated values were stored on a temporary SparseTensor that had no link to the parameter — the sparse embedding gradients were silently dropped.
bugs.invariant: After buffered_allreduce_fallback, param.grad of a sparse-gradient parameter must reflect the all-reduced values (non-zero where local grad was non-zero).

bugs.description: micro_step_id 初始化不一致（构造函数 0 vs backward -1），导致梯度复制/累积条件判断错误，非累积边界时也执行梯度复制而非累积

bugs.root_cause: The base TransformerTrainModule.train_batch unconditionally walked named_parameters and zeroed the first half of expert and router gradients. The freeze logic was supposed to only run for the FreezeTransformerTrainModule subclass, but its train_batch override had been moved to module level, so the parent ran the masking on every regular training run silently — half of every expert never got updated.
